item: the CSRF guard compares the Origin's host and effective port with the Host header's (audit A-001, A-017)
summary: The guard compared only the Origin's hostname with the loopback names, so any other local web app (Origin http://localhost:9999) passed, and a JSON route reached with an untyped body needed no preflight. The Origin (or the Referer when no Origin is sent) must now name the same hostname and the same effective port (80/443 by scheme) as the Host header, the hostname being one the Host guard serves, so OO_ALLOWED_HOSTS names work for a self-hoster's own UI (A-017, documented in SECURITY.md). A non-http(s) scheme or a port that is not a number is refused. 13 red-without tests incl. Referer-only and a no-Content-Type body to /api/system/network; the hostname is compared for EQUALITY with the Host header's (an Origin on 127.0.0.1 against Host localhost is refused), the test client's own host name is not a name an Origin may carry, and behind a TLS proxy OO_ALLOWED_HOSTS plus a proxy that forwards Host and X-Forwarded-Proto is the route (a scheme-hiding proxy is refused). Nothing in src/ checks a request's Content-Type: the Origin check is the only defence on an untyped JSON body, and the test pins it. Not browser-verified.
